M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

scenario_results.description: default-init dispatches the root initial transition to increase and asserts the inlet-valve/pump command outputs required for increase.
scenario_results.name: default_init_enters_increase_outputs

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start in increase probes the inclusive slp <= 0.01 boundary and verifies hold neutralizes both valves.
scenario_results.name: increase_to_hold_at_slp_upper_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start in increase probes just above slp 0.01 so the increase-to-hold guard must not fire.
scenario_results.name: increase_no_fire_just_above_upper_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start in hold probes slp > 0.01 and verifies transition target increase with inlet valve commanded on.
scenario_results.name: hold_to_increase_above_upper_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start in hold probes the non-inclusive slp > 0.01 threshold so exactly 0.01 must not enter increase.
scenario_results.name: hold_no_fire_at_upper_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start in hold probes slp < -0.01 and verifies transition target decrease with return valve and pump release command.
scenario_results.name: hold_to_decrease_below_lower_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start in hold probes the non-inclusive slp < -0.01 threshold so exactly -0.01 must not enter decrease.
scenario_results.name: hold_no_fire_at_lower_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start in decrease probes the inclusive slp >= -0.01 boundary and verifies hold neutralizes valves and pump.
scenario_results.name: decrease_to_hold_at_lower_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start in decrease probes just below slp -0.01 so the decrease-to-hold guard must not fire.
scenario_results.name: decrease_no_fire_below_lower_boundary

evidence: NL states FSM contains increase, hold, decrease; DSL defines System.increase, System.hold, System.decrease.
NL increase sets k1=1,k2=0,n=0; DSL increase enter action assigns k1 = 1; k2 = 0; n = 0.
NL hold sets k1=0,k2=0,n=0; DSL hold enter action assigns k1 = 0; k2 = 0; n = 0.
NL decrease sets k1=0,k2=1,n=500; DSL decrease enter action assigns k1 = 0; k2 = 1; n = 500.
NL guards are increase->hold slp<=0.01, hold->increase slp>0.01, hold->decrease slp<-0.01, decrease->hold slp>=-0.01; DSL contains the same four guarded transitions.
findings.summary: The DSL faithfully represents the NL-described three-state ABS hydraulic supervisor, including state names, valve/pump outputs, and slip-error threshold guards.

evidence: GroundingMap marks variable:slp, variable:k1, variable:k2, variable:n as required.
GroundingMap marks state:increase, state:hold, state:decrease as required.
GroundingMap marks all three enter actions and all four transition guards as required.
inspect_model_to_json_summary reports n_states_leaf=3, n_variables=4, action_count=3, and transition_count=5 including the initial transition.
findings.summary: Required discrete supervisor components are covered: one external slip-error signal, three command outputs, three states, three entry actions, and four threshold transitions.

evidence: NL says wheel speed and vehicle speed are used to compute slip ratio and the PID output drives the Stateflow supervisor.
DSL contains only `slp`, `k1`, `k2`, and `n`; no wheel-speed, vehicle-speed, slip-ratio computation, PID state, PID gain, or controller-output variables are modeled.

GroundingMap assumption states continuous wheel-speed, vehicle-speed, slip-ratio computation, and PID controller are treated as outside the discrete FSM, with `slp` representing the already-computed slip-error signal.
findings.summary: The model abstracts away wheel-speed, vehicle-speed, slip-ratio computation, and PID internals, representing only the Stateflow supervisor input `slp`. This is acceptable for the discrete-supervisor scope but is not a full closed-loop ABS/PID model.

evidence: NL describes a three-state FSM coupled with a PID-based slip controller.
DSL has no continuous dynamics, PID accumulator/integrator/derivative terms, or plant coupling; it only consumes `slp` in guards.
The NL also states continuous wheel-slip dynamics remain in the plant model, which supports this abstraction for the supervisor portion.
findings.summary: The abstraction is intentionally narrow: it captures the discrete hydraulic mode logic but not the coupled continuous/PID behavior referenced by the paper-level NL.

evidence: DSL transitions are limited to the initial transition and the four NL-specified slip-threshold transitions.
No extra fallback, recovery, or exception transition changes valve or pump outputs beyond the specified state entry actions.
findings.summary: No unsafe recovery or hidden fail-open branch is introduced. The DSL contains only the specified normal supervisor transitions and no diagnostic or recovery states.

evidence: design_diagnostics_summary reports W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR for `slp` and W_GUARD_VARS_NEVER_CHANGE on all four guarded transitions.
design_diagnostics_summary.external_input_role_ledger identifies `slp` as an external_input_candidate.
GroundingMap assumption says `slp` represents the already-computed slip-error signal used by the Stateflow supervisor.
findings.summary: `slp` is structurally declared as an ordinary variable even though it is used as an external input from the plant/PID side, producing advisory unchanged-guard warnings. This is a modeling-interface smell rather than an NL-fidelity failure.

evidence: warning_budget_exhausted is empty.
design_diagnostics_summary reports blocking_count=0 and advisory_count=8.
No additional internal update action was added to mutate `slp`, which would have conflicted with the external-input abstraction.
findings.summary: No unjustified repair was applied to silence advisory warnings. The unchanged `slp` guard warnings are consistent with `slp` being an external supervisor input.

evidence: All required FSM states, state outputs, and threshold transitions from the NL are present and simulation scenarios pass 9/9.
The model omits explicit PID and wheel/vehicle speed components described in the paper-level context.
five_component_summary is empty, limiting holistic component-coverage corroboration.
findings.summary: Estimated NFRR tier: T3 for the discrete supervisor abstraction, capped below T4 because the broader PID/plant coupling is represented only by the external `slp` input and the five-component summary is empty.
